issues.failure_explanation: The displayed problem (eq:ivp_ode_weak) — N+1 weak equations plus the pointwise condition q_n(0)=u_n — is not what the scheme solves. Its weak-form matrix [∫φ_p φ_q'] has null vector 1 (rows/columns sum to zero) so the weak equations are generically unsolvable in P_N together with the extra initial condition, while (eq:ivp_ode_weak_rewr_dst) is a square, nonsingular system obtained only after integrating by parts and inserting u_n in the boundary term. The solution of that system does not satisfy the displayed initial condition: the paper's own computation gives q_n(0) = u_n + Δt·Σ_q (a^Tψ)_q F_q with a^Tψ ≠ 0 (e.g. for N=1, a^Tψ = (√3/6, −√3/6)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (eq:ivp_ode_weak) by the problem actually solved: either the N+1 equations (eq:ivp_ode_weak_rewr_dst), or the weak form obtained after integration by parts in which u_n enters the left (upwind) boundary term together with the trace value q_n(0^+); delete the false pointwise initial condition and reword the places that invoke it.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the local solution is the solution of the stated weak IVP with initial condition q_n(0)=u_n is false, and the derivation 'evaluating (eq:ivp_ode_weak) leads to (eq:ivp_ode_weak_rewr_dst)' is not an equivalence. The scheme itself and all order/stability results obtained from the RK reformulation are unaffected.
issues.title: Local DG predictor does not solve the stated weak initial-value problem
issues.why_classification: A correct formulation must withdraw the promised pointwise initial condition and replace the defining weak problem by a different (flux-type) statement, i.e. a limited weakening plus a re-derivation of the construction; no order, stability or rate guarantee is lost, and no new global proof architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: For N=1 the tableau prints a_12 = −(1−√3)/2 and a_21 = (1−√3)/2. From the source's definitions (κ_pq = ψ_pψ_q + ∫φ_p φ_q', μ = diag(1/2,1/2)) one gets κ = [[1,(√3−1)/2],[−(1+√3)/2,1]] and a = κ^{-1}μ = [[1/3,(1−√3)/6],[(1+√3)/6,1/3]]. The printed rows sum to (3√3−1)/6 and (1−3√3)/6 instead of the abscissas τ_0=(3−√3)/6, τ_1=(3+√3)/6, contradicting the paper's own relation Σ_q a_pq = τ_p (case r=0 of C(N)); the printed matrix therefore defines an inconsistent, first-order method. The N=2 and N=3 tableaux do satisfy κa = μ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the two off-diagonal entries of the N=1 tableau as a = κ^{-1}μ, i.e. a = [[1/3,(1−√3)/6],[(1+√3)/6,1/3]].

In that regime the conjunct N > L is false, so the equivalence says nothing about the stage values and the conclusion does not follow. This unsupported conclusion is the only analytic argument offered for the failure of C(N+1) (and D(N+1)), which Corollary coroll:rk_is_not_coll and the surrounding prose rely on (only numerical evidence is given elsewhere).

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses B(2N+2), C(N), D(N) give only the Butcher lower bound p ≥ min(2N+2, 2N+2, 2N+1) = 2N+1; no order condition of degree 2N+2 is shown to fail, so the equality p_RK = 2N+1 (and with it the comparison 'one unit less than the GL method') is not established. issues.failure_explanation: The proof computes only degrees/ranks and then asserts the Padé identity; knowing that deg P ≤ N and deg Q = N+1 does not identify R(z) with the (N,N+1)-Padé approximant, which additionally requires that R(z) match exp(z) through order 2N+2 (never verified). The degree statements themselves are wrong: a is invertible, so det(I−za) has degree N+1 (not N), and rank(a−1w^T)=N gives numerator degree at most N (not N−1); the asserted degrees (N−1 over N) would give error O(z^{2N}), contradicting the O(z^{2N+2}) used in Corollary cor:added-3.
